summary: Hardened the bounded log subject (SEC-21.5-02, SEC-21.5-03) in src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs. Create(Guid, string?) now takes the final path component as the substring after the last '/' or the last '\', whichever is later, on every host (the host-platform Path.GetFileName call and the System.IO using are gone), re-runs the empty/whitespace check on the extracted component, and keeps the post-normalization item-id fallback; Create(Guid) is unchanged. NormalizeFileName's removal predicate is now exactly the documented non-printing set Cc, Cf, Zl, and Zp (a superset of the pre-fix Rune.IsControl/Cc-only predicate) in the unchanged single scalar-wise pass, with MaximumScalarValues = 128 applied after removal, surrogate pairs never split, and whitespace never collapsed or trimmed; the exact category set is stated in the XML doc comments and in a new ADR-026 implementation note (Decision clauses 1-5 untouched). LogSubjectTests grows from 23 to 52 cases. The pre-fix probe against the unmodified source is Failed 25, Passed 27, Total 52; the same focused run after the fix is 52/52. Default suite Failed 0, Passed 1966, Skipped 66, Total 2032 and host-guarded suite Failed 0, Passed 1986, Skipped 46, Total 2032 (both +29 passed / +29 total, exactly the 29 added cases, vs the 21.10 tree); LogRedactionTests 167/167; no committed renderer golden, RenderVersion, or renderer-schema change.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given a media path whose file-name component carries a Unicode Cf format character (for example U+202E or U+200B) or a Zl/Zp separator (U+2028/U+2029), the emitted log subject contains no such scalar; an ordinary Cc control is still stripped, so the removal predicate is a superset of the pre-fix behavior rather than a replacement.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: LogSubject.NormalizeFileName routes every scalar through IsNonPrintingScalar, which matches exactly UnicodeCategory.Control, Format, LineSeparator, and ParagraphSeparator (src/ArrTags/Logging/LogSubject.cs, IsNonPrintingScalar). LogSubjectTests.UnicodeNonPrintingScalarsAreRemoved covers U+202E, U+200B, U+200D, U+00AD, U+202A, U+202C, U+2066, U+2069, U+2028, and U+2029; NonPrintingRemovalStillRemovesOrdinaryControlScalars proves Cc (U+0001/U+0000) is still stripped alongside U+202E; all of these fail on the pre-fix code (probe: Failed 25).

acceptance_criteria.criterion: Given 'C:\Users\admin\Videos\secret.mkv', the subject is 'secret.mkv' and contains no backslash, no account name, and no directory component; the same holds for a UNC path and a mixed-separator path, on the pinned Linux host and on any host.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: LogSubject.ExtractFinalComponent uses only path.LastIndexOf('/') and path.LastIndexOf('\\') (no host-platform API); LogSubjectTests.FinalComponentIsTakenOnBothSeparators covers the drive path, the UNC path '\\fileserver\media\secret\file.mkv', the mixed 'C:/Users\admin/Videos/secret.mkv', a relative backslash path, and '/media\Movies/mixed.mkv'; WindowsStylePathEmitsNoAccountOrDirectoryComponent asserts no backslash, 'admin', 'Users', 'Videos', or 'C:' in the subject. The drive/UNC/relative cases fail on the pre-fix code.

acceptance_criteria.criterion: The 128 Unicode-scalar bound still holds after the widened removal (a 300-scalar name still truncates to exactly 128), the single pass still never splits a surrogate pair, and whitespace is still neither collapsed nor trimmed.
acceptance_criteria.evidence: BoundIsAppliedAfterNonPrintingRemoval (150 leading U+202E/U+200B pairs then 300 'a's) asserts exactly 128 'a' scalars; WidenedRemovalStillNeverSplitsASurrogatePair asserts 128 astral U+1F3AC scalars / 256 UTF-16 units after a leading U+202E; NonPrintingRemovalDoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace asserts 'my  movie .mkv' from 'my <U+202E> movie .mkv'; the pre-existing NameAtTheBoundIsEmittedUnchanged, NameBeyondTheBoundIsTruncatedToTheScalarBound, BoundNeverSplitsASurrogatePair, ControlRemovalDoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace, and BoundIsAppliedAfterControlRemoval all still pass unchanged.

test_sensitivity: SEC-21.5-02: with the unmodified LogSubject.cs, UnicodeNonPrintingScalarsAreRemoved fails for all 10 scalars (U+202E, U+200B, U+200D, U+00AD, U+202A, U+202C, U+2066, U+2069, U+2028, U+2029 - observed as 'movie<scalar>.mkv' rather than 'movie.mkv'), NonPrintingRemovalStillRemovesOrdinaryControlScalars fails ('mo<U+202E>vie.mkv'), NonPrintingRemovalPreservesOtherCharactersVerbatim fails ('お気に入り<U+202E>Cafe<combining>🎬.mkv'), NonPrintingRemovalDoesNotCollapseOrTrimWhitespace fails, BoundIsAppliedAfterNonPrintingRemoval fails (leading U+202E/U+200B emitted), WidenedRemovalStillNeverSplitsASurrogatePair fails, and the 3 NamesThatReduceToNothingAfterNonPrintingRemovalFallBackToTheItemIdentifier cases fail (Cf-only name emitted instead of the item id). Each assertion depends on the widened predicate, so removing IsNonPrintingScalar (reverting to Rune.IsControl) makes them fail.

SEC-21.5-03: with the unmodified LogSubject.cs (host-platform Path.GetFileName on the pinned Linux host), FinalComponentIsTakenOnBothSeparators fails for 'C:\Users\admin\Videos\secret.mkv', '\\fileserver\media\secret\file.mkv', and 'relative\folder\Episode.S01E01.mkv' (the whole string is emitted, observed with 32 and 34 scalars for the drive and UNC paths), WindowsStylePathEmitsNoAccountOrDirectoryComponent fails ('admin', 'Users', 'Videos', 'C:' present), and the separator-only 'C:\', '\', '\\fileserver\share\' cases fail. Replacing ExtractFinalComponent's dual-separator max(LastIndexOf) with the pre-fix Path.GetFileName makes them fail again.

Positive controls that pass both pre- and post-fix and therefore prove the change is a superset rather than a replacement: an ordinary Cc control is still stripped (ControlScalarsAreRemoved, NonPrintingRemovalStillRemovesOrdinaryControlScalars' Cc half), non-ASCII/decomposed-combining/astral text is preserved verbatim (NonAsciiNameIsEmittedVerbatim, NonPrintingRemovalPreservesOtherCharactersVerbatim' preserve half), whitespace is not collapsed or trimmed, the 128-scalar bound cases, the POSIX component/fallback cases, and the URL-shaped SR-15.4-04 case.

The mixed-separator 'C:/Users\admin/Videos/secret.mkv' and '/media\Movies/mixed.mkv' and the separator-only '\/' theory cases pass on the pre-fix code as well (their last '/' is later than the last '\'), so they are not claimed as discriminating; they pin the dual-separator rule's later-separator ordering.

No new production behaviour is left unprobed: the pre-fix probe run is the recorded evidence that every new case is discriminating, and all probes were run against the committed test file with only the production source differing.

interpretations.question: Which exact Unicode categories the widened removal predicate should cover (the task requires at minimum Cc/Cf/Zl/Zp and asks for the exclusion decision to be recorded).
interpretations.chosen: Exactly Cc (Control), Cf (Format), Zl (LineSeparator), and Zp (ParagraphSeparator). All other categories are preserved, notably Zs (space separators), Mn (combining marks), Co (private use), and Cn (unassigned).
interpretations.basis: Acceptance criterion 3 and the required work require whitespace never collapsed/trimmed and combining/non-ASCII/astral text preserved verbatim; acceptance criterion 1 requires Cc still stripped; 'at minimum' plus the plan's instruction to exclude an ambiguous category explicitly rather than implicitly.
interpretations.impact: Log output only; no persisted authoritative state, user-visible configuration, or limit/window/unit semantics change. A private-use or unassigned scalar is still emitted, bounded to 128 scalars.

interpretations.question: Whether an accepted ADR-026 clause authorizes widening the removal predicate beyond literal Cc-only 'control characters' (clause 2 says 'has control characters removed, and is otherwise emitted verbatim').
interpretations.chosen: Treated as an implementation correction authorized by the recorded user decision, not an amendment: the user chose to fix SEC-21.5-02 and SEC-21.5-03 rather than accept them (PLANS.md Phase 21 corrective paragraph and docs/implementation/planning/v1.2-phase-21-log-subject-correction.json, which states SEC-21.5-02 is a narrowing of what clause 2 permits being emitted and both fixes move toward the accepted decision). ADR-026's Decision clauses were not edited; the new implementation note records the shipped behavior and supersedes the earlier reading-level notes.
interpretations.basis: Task constraint: 'If you conclude an accepted ADR-026 clause does not authorize widening the predicate, STOP and report NEEDS_USER_INPUT.' The corrective record explicitly resolves the point and the user decision is recorded there and in PLANS.md, so the stop condition does not apply.
interpretations.impact: None beyond the subject's own output; the supersession is recorded rather than silently implied.

interpretations.question: What happens to a POSIX file name that legitimately contains a backslash (legal on Linux), now that both separators are always split.
interpretations.chosen: The subject is truncated to the text after the last backslash (a strictly shorter subject); the full name is not emitted.
interpretations.basis: The required work fixes the extraction as 'the substring after the last / and after the last \, whichever is later', and the corrective record's risk note records the truncation as the intended fail-toward-safety direction.
interpretations.impact: A rare Linux file name's subject is shortened, never lengthened; no secret or directory chain can be reintroduced.

interpretations.chosen: README's 'host-native media path' qualifier was corrected to the separator-independent wording (the qualifier existed only because of the pre-fix host semantics). docs/limitations/accepted.md was left unchanged, with the check recorded above.
interpretations.basis: README's qualifier was added by task 15.4 precisely to scope the exclusion to host separator semantics (docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md Phase 15) and became obsolete with this fix; the limitations register explicitly is not changed by this corrective chain per docs/implementation/planning/v1.2-phase-21-log-subject-correction.json ('no limitations register entry is created, changed, or removed by this chain'), and its statement remains true.
interpretations.impact: User-facing guide wording only; no behaviour or status fact changes.
